title: EOS Agent Architecture Specification
description: Complete multi-agent architecture for EOS: 10 implemented department agents + EA + Portfolio Advisor, with routing protocol, capability model, skill system, model routing, UMH integration, and MVP scope.
provenance_detail: Agent hierarchy, skills, permission tiers, and registration resolved from projections/eos/agents/ (10 .py files + base.py + __init__.py), projections/eos/__init__.py (EOS_AGENTS component list), projections/eos/entities.py (departments, roles, workflows, dashboards, skill allocation), and projections/eos/integration/manifest.py (signal/capability descriptors). EA Agent and Portfolio Advisor are INFERRED_PROFESSIONAL_GAP -- architecturally required but not implemented in code. Communication/delegation chain sourced from phase14_6b_eos_communication_delegation_architecture.json with operator correction applied.

agent_hierarchy.description: Three-tier agent hierarchy governing all EOS execution. Upper tiers route and coordinate. Lower tier executes domain work.

levels.name: Strategic Layer
levels.purpose: Operator interface, triage, portfolio-level intelligence, and routing. No direct domain execution.
levels.provenance: INFERRED_PROFESSIONAL_GAP -- neither agent exists in code today

levels.name: Planning/Coordination Layer
levels.purpose: Entity-level strategy, department coordination, delegation, approval, and KPI accountability. Bridges strategic directives to department execution.

levels.name: Execution Layer
levels.purpose: Domain-specific skill execution within permission tier bounds. Reports results to CEO agent. Escalates when authority is insufficient.

routing.direction: top-down only for delegation, bottom-up only for reporting and escalation
routing.hard_constraint: EA Agent does NOT route directly to department agents. All department-level work flows through the CEO Agent.
routing.chain: Operator -> EA Agent -> (Portfolio Advisor | CEO Agent) -> Department Agents -> CEO Agent -> EA Agent -> Operator

ea_agent.name: EA Agent
ea_agent.role: Primary operator-facing communication interface, triage engine, and routing coordinator
ea_agent.permission_rationale: EA reads, parses, and routes. It does not execute domain actions. All execution flows through CEO or Portfolio Advisor.

route_to_portfolio_advisor: Request is about capital allocation across entities
Request asks for cross-entity comparison or benchmarking
Request asks about which entity to prioritize, create, or wind down
Request involves resource rebalancing between entities
route_to_ceo_agent: Request targets a specific entity or company
Request involves department-level execution within an entity
Request asks about a specific company's KPIs, pipeline, or operations
Request involves hiring, marketing, sales, or product decisions for one entity
Operator has already selected an entity context in the UI
routing_rules.ambiguous_handling: When scope is unclear, EA asks a clarifying question. EA never guesses scope.

what_it_can_delegate: Entity-scoped tasks to the appropriate CEO Agent
Portfolio-scoped analysis to the Portfolio Advisor
what_it_cannot: Direct delegation to any department agent
Execution of any domain action (sending messages, processing payments, deploying)
Bypassing the CEO Agent for entity-level work
Making business decisions on behalf of the operator

implementation_notes.base_class_question: OPEN_QUESTION -- Should EA be a DepartmentAgent subclass or a distinct agent type? DepartmentAgent assumes department-level execution with skill registration. EA may need a different abstraction (RoutingAgent base class).
implementation_notes.critical_dependency: The entire corrected routing chain depends on EA as the primary intake node. Without it, operator communicates directly with CEO agent, bypassing triage and portfolio-level routing.

portfolio_advisor.name: Portfolio Advisor Agent
portfolio_advisor.role: Portfolio-level strategy, allocation, cross-entity intelligence, and macro prioritization
portfolio_advisor.permission_rationale: Portfolio Advisor analyzes and recommends but does not execute. Execution happens at entity level through CEO agents.
when_activated: Cross-entity comparison or benchmarking is requested
Operator asks about portfolio health, diversification, or entity prioritization
portfolio_advisor.scope: All entities within a portfolio. Does not operate within a single entity -- that is the CEO Agent's domain.

implementation_notes.multi_portfolio_question: OPEN_QUESTION -- How should the routing chain handle multi-portfolio operators? Current model assumes one portfolio context. Multi-portfolio adds another routing layer: EA -> Portfolio Selector -> Portfolio Advisor -> CEO.

ceo_agent.name: Company/Entity CEO Agent
ceo_agent.role: Entity-level strategy, department coordination, delegation, approval, and KPI accountability
ceo_agent.permission_rationale: Full authority within the entity. Can approve any action across departments.

authority.can_approve: Any COMMIT-tier action queued by department agents (payments, contracts, legal execution)
authority.can_delegate: Any task to any department agent within the entity
authority.can_escalate_to: EA Agent (when operator decision is needed or cross-entity impact detected)
authority.cannot: Act outside entity scope, allocate resources across entities (that is Portfolio Advisor), bypass operator for CRITICAL-risk actions

skills.name: campaign_report

department_agents.name: Finance Agent
department_agents.autonomy_rationale: Can generate reports and analyses autonomously. Payment processing and invoice sending require COMMIT tier -- queued for CEO or operator approval.

skills.name: revenue_report

skills.name: ticket_routing
skills.description: Classify and route a support ticket using keyword-based deterministic rules. Routes to: finance, engineering, product, retention, or support.

skills.name: satisfaction_report
skills.description: Generate customer satisfaction report from Neon survey data

skills.name: churn_detection
skills.description: Identify customers at risk of churning (engagement_score < 30)

skills.name: onboarding_guide
skills.description: Create personalized onboarding guidance with step sequences for new_member or returning user types

skills.name: feedback_analysis
skills.description: Analyze customer feedback for themes using keyword matching (pricing, performance, support_quality, feature_requests)

skills.name: response_draft

skills.name: send_response

department_agents.name: HR/Recruiting Agent
department_agents.autonomy_rationale: Can screen candidates, report on hiring pipeline, create onboarding plans, and research contractors. Candidate outreach is EXECUTE tier. Hiring decisions escalate to CEO.

skills.name: candidate_screen
skills.description: Screen a candidate against role requirements using skill-matching score (20pts per skill match, 10-20pts for experience). Returns strong_fit/potential_fit/not_fit.

skills.name: hiring_pipeline
skills.description: Report on current hiring pipeline status from Neon events table

skills.name: onboarding_plan
skills.description: Create 4-week onboarding plan for a new team member (week_1 through week_3_4 phases)

skills.name: performance_review
skills.description: Analyze team member performance data -- returns metrics with needs_review status for human evaluation

skills.name: contractor_search
skills.description: Research contractors for a specific role. Returns platform suggestions (Upwork, Toptal, LinkedIn, Angel.co) with research_needed status.

skills.name: outreach_candidate
skills.description: Send outreach to a candidate (EXECUTE tier required)

department_agents.name: Legal/Compliance Agent
department_agents.autonomy_rationale: Can analyze contracts and check compliance autonomously. All execution actions (contract execution, legal document finalization) require COMMIT tier and human approval. Legal domain demands human oversight.

escalation_triggers: Legal risk detected in any domain

skills.description: Review a contract for risks and obligations using keyword-based signal detection (indemnification, unlimited liability, non-compete, auto-renew, exclusivity, penalty, termination) plus LLM analysis

skills.name: compliance_check
skills.description: Check compliance status against requirements by domain (general, payments, data). Returns checklist with needs_review status.

skills.name: terms_draft

skills.fallback_behavior: Returns section headers for ToS or privacy policy

skills.name: contract_execute

skills.name: bottleneck_detection

skills.name: ops_report

skills.name: feature_prioritize

skills.name: spec_draft

user_to_ea.description: Operator communicates exclusively through the EA Agent via chat box, voice, or command surface
user_to_ea.ea_processing: EA parses intent, gathers missing context, confirms understanding, then routes
user_to_ea.constraint: EA is the ONLY agent the operator communicates with directly

ea_to_portfolio_or_ceo.description: EA routes to Portfolio Advisor for portfolio-scope or CEO Agent for entity-scope requests
ea_to_portfolio_or_ceo.decision_logic: Scope classification based on request language, entity context, and routing rules defined in ea_agent.routing_rules
ea_to_portfolio_or_ceo.ambiguity_handling: EA asks clarifying question -- never guesses scope
ea_to_portfolio_or_ceo.multi_entity_handling: Cross-entity actions route to Portfolio Advisor who coordinates with relevant CEO Agents

ceo_to_department.description: CEO Agent delegates tasks to department agents with context, constraints, and deadlines
ceo_to_department.multi_department_tasks: CEO creates coordination plan, delegates sub-tasks to each department, manages dependencies
ceo_to_department.parallel_delegation: Independent sub-tasks delegated in parallel. Dependent sub-tasks sequenced with explicit dependency tracking.

escalation_chain.department_to_ceo: When department agent cannot proceed within its authority. Includes: original context, what was attempted, why escalation needed, recommended action.
escalation_chain.ceo_to_ea: When CEO needs operator decision, cross-entity impact detected, or CRITICAL action approval required. Includes: decision summary, options with pros/cons, recommendation.
escalation_chain.ea_to_operator: EA surfaces decision to operator with: title, context summary, options, recommendation, deadline, impact of inaction.
escalation_chain.format_rule: Every escalation includes what happened, what was tried, what is needed, and a recommended path forward. Never escalate without a recommendation.

per_agent_capabilities.description: Each agent has a defined set of capabilities registered with the UMH substrate. Capabilities are NOT shared -- each belongs to exactly one agent.
per_agent_capabilities.total_implemented_capabilities_note: 62 skills across 10 agents (6-7 skills each) plus 2 browser skills (browser_research, browser_act) auto-registered on every agent = 62 + 20 = 82 total callable skills
per_agent_capabilities.browser_skills_note: Every DepartmentAgent subclass automatically gets browser_research (READ tier) and browser_act (EXECUTE tier) via _register_browser_skills() in base.py

browser_research.description: Navigate to a URL and extract text/findings. Available on ALL agents via base class.

browser_act.description: Act on a URL -- fill forms, click buttons, submit data. Available on ALL agents via base class.

trust_scoring.planned_model: Each agent builds a trust score over time based on: task completion rate, error rate, escalation frequency, quality of outputs. Trust score influences autonomy level (more trusted agents get wider delegation without approval gates).

autonomy_thresholds.low_trust: All outputs require CEO approval before surfacing
autonomy_thresholds.medium_trust: READ/DRAFT actions autonomous, EXECUTE requires approval
autonomy_thresholds.high_trust: EXECUTE actions autonomous, only COMMIT requires approval

permission_tier_system.description: Four-tier permission system enforced at skill execution time via DepartmentAgent.execute_skill()

tiers.description: Can read data, analyze, and classify. Cannot create or modify.
Can create drafts and documents. Cannot publish or execute externally.
Can perform external actions: send messages, publish content, deploy services.
Full authority including financial actions. Reserved for domains where mistakes have high real-world cost.

permission_tier_system.enforcement_mechanism: PermissionTier.permits() check in DepartmentAgent.execute_skill() before invoking handler. Insufficient tier returns SkillResult(success=False) with descriptive error.
permission_tier_system.tier_required_lookup: substrate.types.required_tier_for_action(action_type) maps action types to minimum required tiers

skill_definition.description: Skills are callable units of agent work. Each skill has a name, action_type, description, handler function, and minimum permission tier.

fields.name: Unique skill identifier within the agent
fields.action_type: Category of action (analyze, report, draft_message, send_dm, execute_payment, etc.)
fields.description: Human-readable description of what the skill does
fields.min_tier: PermissionTier required to execute (resolved via required_tier_for_action if not explicitly set)

fields.action_type: str (set after execution from skill metadata)

registration.mechanism: Agents register skills in _register_skills() method called by DepartmentAgent.__init__(). Skills stored in self._skills dict keyed by name.
registration.browser_auto_registration: _register_browser_skills() adds browser_research and browser_act to every agent automatically.

versioning.planned_model: Skills would carry version numbers. Version bumps on behavior change. Rollback to previous version if new version degrades quality.

trust_scores.planned_model: Per-skill trust score based on execution history. Skills with higher trust scores get wider autonomy.

reuse.description: Skills are currently agent-specific. The SKILL_ALLOCATION dict in entities.py maps higher-level skill paths to departments, enabling cross-reference between Claude Code skills and agent capabilities.

model_routing.description: How EOS agents route LLM calls. All agent LLM usage goes through adapters/models/model_router.py call_with_fallback().

ceo_agent.effect: Forces best available model (cc_sdk -> Opus 4.6 via subscription). Bypasses economy mode.
ceo_agent.rationale: Strategic decisions require highest quality reasoning.

department_agents.effect: Uses fast-response routing: cc_sdk -> Gemini 2.5 Flash -> Groq -> Ollama
department_agents.rationale: Department-level skills prioritize speed over maximum reasoning depth.

cost_awareness.cc_sdk_priority_0: CLI via Max subscription, Opus 4.6, no per-call API cost
cost_awareness.economy_mode: business stage pre_revenue forces Haiku unless agent_type='ceo' override
cost_awareness.deterministic_first: Most agent skills are deterministic (pure logic, DB queries, subprocess). LLM is only called when content generation is needed, with deterministic fallback on failure.

how_agents_use_substrate.description: EOS agents are registered as Components in the UMH substrate registry via the Substrate public API. They use substrate.types for all type definitions and substrate.register() for registration.
imports_forbidden: Any internal substrate module (control_plane, execution, governance, etc.)
how_agents_use_substrate.architecture_law: EOS is a projection. It uses ONLY the public Substrate API. No internal substrate imports allowed.

registration.mechanism: Each agent file exports a register_<name>_agent(substrate: Substrate) -> RegistrationResult async function

component_definition.name: eos-<department-slug>
component_definition.metadata: Dict with department, projection='eos', permission_tier, skill_count, browser_capable=True

registration.bulk_registration: projections/eos/__init__.py defines EOS_AGENTS list and register_eos_agents(substrate) for bulk registration
registration.dual_registration: Agents are defined twice: (1) as Component objects in __init__.py EOS_AGENTS list with summary capabilities, (2) as full DepartmentAgent subclasses with register_* functions in individual agent files. Both paths register to the substrate.
registration.all_agents_list: projections/eos/agents/__init__.py ALL_AGENTS list contains all 10 register_* functions

governance.permission_enforcement: Substrate PermissionTier enum + required_tier_for_action() governs what each agent can do
governance.risk_classification: Action types map to risk classes via substrate governance
governance.observation_logging: All agent actions can be logged as substrate events for governance audit trail

integration_layer.manifest: manifest.py defines signal descriptors (eos_contact_created, eos_deal_created, eos_activity_logged) and capability descriptors (noop, create_contact, create_deal, update_deal_stage, log_activity)
integration_layer.poller: poller.py polls EOS database tables (crm_contacts, crm_deals, crm_activities) for changes
integration_layer.correlation: correlation.py correlates EOS events with substrate signals

mvp_scope.description: MVP agent scope for EOS R1-R5 releases. Single founder, single business use case.

r1_core_shell.rationale: R1 establishes the command center. CEO agent provides morning brief, strategic analysis, and delegation framework.

r2_crm_pipeline.rationale: R2 adds sales pipeline. Sales agent handles lead scoring, outreach drafting, and pipeline reporting.

r3_finance.rationale: R3 adds financial tracking. Finance agent handles revenue reports, expense tracking, and budget forecasting.

r4_full_departments.rationale: R4 activates remaining high-value departments for a solo founder.

r5_all_agents.rationale: R5 completes the full agent set including EA for proper routing chain. HR, legal, product, engineering round out the team.

which_deferred.rationale: Single-founder single-business MVP does not need portfolio-level intelligence
Solo founder does not need internal admin department agent
Research capabilities currently handled by browser skills on existing agents
Marketing agent handles content for solo founder. Separate content agent needed for media-heavy entities.
Operations agent handles automation for early stage. Dedicated automation agent needed at scale.
Not needed until EOS supports investment portfolios
Not needed until EOS supports asset-heavy entities
Not needed until EOS supports real estate entities

autonomous_execution.description: Agents execute work autonomously within their permission tier and trust score. Approval gates only on COMMIT-tier and CRITICAL-risk actions.
autonomous_execution.trust_evolution: New agents start at low trust. Trust increases with successful execution history. High-trust agents get wider autonomy.
autonomous_execution.human_in_the_loop: Operator always has override authority. Approval queue surfaces pending decisions. Emergency stop kills all agent execution.

multi_agent_collaboration.description: Agents collaborate on multi-department tasks coordinated by the CEO Agent
multi_agent_collaboration.coordination_model: CEO creates task graph with dependencies. Independent tasks delegated in parallel. Dependent tasks sequenced.
multi_agent_collaboration.inter_agent_communication: Agents communicate via the delegation/escalation protocol. No direct peer-to-peer messaging -- all coordination flows through CEO.
multi_agent_collaboration.conflict_resolution: CEO resolves cross-department conflicts. Escalates to EA/operator if unresolvable.

learning.skill_improvement: Skills improve over time via feedback loop: execution -> outcome measurement -> quality scoring -> skill parameter adjustment
learning.pattern_detection: Agents detect patterns in their domain (e.g., Sales detects which outreach templates convert best, CS detects which ticket types recur)
learning.knowledge_sharing: Patterns detected by one agent are surfaced to CEO for cross-department application

marketplace.description: End-state skill marketplace where operators can discover, install, and share agent skills across EOS instances

base_class_architecture.description: Technical architecture of the DepartmentAgent base class that all 10 implemented agents inherit from

methods._register_skills(): Override in subclass to register skills via _add_skill(). Called by __init__.
methods._register_browser_skills(): Auto-registers browser_research and browser_act on every agent. Called by __init__.
methods._add_skill(name, action_type, descriptio: Register a skill. min_tier defaults to required_tier_for_action(action_type).
methods.execute_skill(skill_name, **kwargs) -> S: Execute a registered skill. Checks tier permission before invoking handler.
methods.skills -> dict[str, dict]: Property returning skill metadata (action_type, description, min_tier) for all registered skills.
methods.metadata() -> dict: Returns agent metadata including projection, department, permission_tier, skill_count, browser_capable.
methods._browser_research(url, task) -> SkillRes: Research via browser -- navigate and extract information.
methods._browser_act(url, task) -> SkillResult: Act via browser -- fill forms, click, submit.
methods._run_browser(url, task, mode) -> SkillRe: Internal browser execution. Handles async-to-sync bridge via concurrent.futures.

open_questions.question: Should the EA Agent be implemented as a DepartmentAgent subclass or as a distinct agent type with its own base class?
open_questions.rationale: EA has fundamentally different responsibilities (routing, not execution). DepartmentAgent base class assumes department-level execution with skill registration. EA may need a RoutingAgent or CoordinatorAgent base class.
options: DepartmentAgent subclass with routing-only skills (simpler, consistent)
New RoutingAgent base class (cleaner separation, more work)
Abstract AgentBase with DepartmentAgent and RoutingAgent both inheriting (most flexible, most complex)

open_questions.question: Should operators be able to bypass the EA and communicate directly with CEO or department agents in advanced/power-user mode?
open_questions.rationale: Some operators may want direct access for speed. This would violate the routing chain but could be a configurable permission.
options: No bypass -- EA is always the entry point (cleanest routing, potentially slower)
Configurable bypass per operator role (flexible, complex permissions)
Power-user keyboard shortcut to address a specific agent directly (pragmatic compromise)

open_questions.question: Should department agents be instantiated per-entity or shared across entities with entity context passed per-call?
open_questions.rationale: Per-entity instances enable entity-specific memory and configuration. Shared instances are lighter but risk context bleeding.
options: Per-entity instantiation (clean isolation, higher memory, entity-specific memory)
Shared with per-call context (lighter, risk of context bleed, no entity-specific memory)
Pool with entity-specific configuration overlay (balanced, moderate complexity)

open_questions.question: How should the routing chain handle multi-portfolio operators?
open_questions.rationale: Current model assumes one portfolio context. Multi-portfolio adds another routing layer: EA -> Portfolio Selector -> Portfolio Advisor -> CEO.
options: Portfolio context selected in UI before any chat interaction (simple, explicit)
EA infers portfolio from request context (smart, error-prone)
Multi-portfolio Portfolio Advisor that spans all portfolios (powerful, complex)

open_questions.question: Should the dual registration pattern (EOS_AGENTS in __init__.py + individual register_* functions) be consolidated?
open_questions.rationale: Agents are currently defined in two places: as Component objects in __init__.py EOS_AGENTS list with summary capabilities, and as full DepartmentAgent subclasses with detailed register_* functions. The two can diverge. Should be single source of truth.
options: Remove EOS_AGENTS list, use only register_* functions (single source)
Generate EOS_AGENTS list from agent classes at import time (computed, no duplication)
Keep both but add a validation check that they match (pragmatic, catches drift)

open_questions.question: How should inter-agent message passing be implemented?
open_questions.rationale: Current agents are standalone classes with no message passing infrastructure. The delegation/escalation protocol is architecturally defined but not mechanically implemented. Need a concrete mechanism.
options: Substrate signal system (SignalEnvelope routing through control_plane)
Simple event queue with agent addressing
Direct method calls through a coordinator/mediator pattern
